title: The Doghouse
slugLine: A cash-flow analysis of a Culver City dog grooming and spa business, with three cases and a plan to restart its growth.

research.problem: The business ==broke even one month after launch==, but **its growth has stalled**: with no marketing and an owner unwilling to raise funds, cash is not keeping up with inflation.

stakeholders.name: Local dog owners
stakeholders.note: Culver City, many of them repeat customers

stakeholders.name: Vets, dog trainers and pet stores

painPoints.label: Stalled growth
painPoints.detail: Repeat customers and low marginal costs gave steady cash growth after launch, then it flattened into stagnation.

painPoints.label: No marketing
painPoints.detail: There is no marketing team. Seasonal events and discounts are the only marketing, and holiday events attract only local customers.

painPoints.label: An unknown CAC
painPoints.detail: Without marketing spend, the business cannot tell what it costs to win a customer.

painPoints.label: Inflation
painPoints.detail: Stagnant revenue cannot keep up with inflation.

insights.insight: Grooming and bathing earn about the same
insights.evidence: Grooming brings 45.8% of revenue and bathing 45.4%, but grooming takes longer and is more popular. The ideal ratio of grooms to baths for profit is 2:13.
The handmade bandannas and ribbons included with each groom are well liked.

insights.insight: Each groomer earns far more than they cost
insights.evidence: A single employee generates $2,700 a week at optimal efficiency against a $960 weekly payroll.

design.lead: Three cases model where the cash goes next: the base case, an optimistic case driven by referrals, and a conservative case where churn and inflation wear the cash down.

items.label: Dematting, flea removal, dyeing and more

clauses.label: Base
clauses.text: Break-even one month after launch; repeat customers, low marginal costs and a risk-averse owner give steady cash growth, then stagnation.

clauses.label: Optimistic
clauses.text: An effective referral system grows monthly customers exponentially and adds cash without raising marketing costs, for a stable, effectively unlimited runway.

clauses.label: Conservative
clauses.text: Churn, inflation and no marketing spend turn stagnation into decline after an inflection point in February, leaving a dangerous runway of about 6–8 months.

results.lead: One more employee and a second station ==pay for themselves in 3–4 weeks==, and new revenue streams can fund the marketing that restarts growth.

blocks.title: Adding a second station

rows.label: Revenue per employee, at optimal efficiency
Extra bathing station and grooming table

blocks.note: Other marginal costs, such as utilities and G&A, are negligible.

blocks.title: Recommendations
items: Spend on marketing to learn the business’s CAC
Try social media or referral marketing to restart customer growth, then keep the channel that works best (social and influencer marketing is the norm for dog groomers)
Sell the handmade accessories on their own, perhaps even B2B
Partner with vets, dog trainers and pet stores for referral-based revenue without bringing those services in-house
Put the extra revenue into marketing to stay ahead of inflation
